about: Born, Not Made, simplified version after the sketch of 21 November 2026. Frame: x toward the opening, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor (the tank floor is 3 mm lower).

stages.name: Dock
stages.text: The tail docks to the head from behind, sliding along the floor; three disc magnets close the thin docking ring.

stages.name: Unfold, gel
stages.text: The arm unfolds and injects the gel: 2.2 L at 0.1 L per minute. This is the first fill; the gel then stays in the box from birth to birth. Then the water comes in.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The electromagnet picks the electronics kit once, from the store in the tail, carries the kit over the rear wall of the gel box and places the kit in the gel, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change in the tail: holder off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release). The needle then crosses the rear wall of the gel box from above.

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the folded newborn around the kit: 45 m of bead, 0.08 L of Dragon Skin 10 NV.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Air in, nose up
stages.text: The ball needle enters the valve. Air pushes the trapped gel out of the folds, the newborn floats up in the gel, and the arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the lip.

stages.name: Push while inflating
stages.text: The arm steers the tail end from above and pushes; the newborn slides over the lip, and each segment opens outside. No contractions.

stages.name: Hold and fill
stages.text: The arm holds, the newborn fills to full size, the needle lets go.

stages.name: Float
stages.text: The newborn floats in the water: gravity, buoyancy, drag, a damped settling.

stages.name: Swim
stages.text: The newborn swims straight ahead on one small jet.

notes: The tail slides forward along the tank floor and docks to the head from behind. Everything for the tools rides in the tail, behind the docking plane. Three magnets close the dry seam.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, over the gel box. The base does not move.
Gel comes through the line on the arm; the arm moves the outlet over three fill points.
With the gel in, the tank is filled with water to 93 mm.
The bare arm folds back into the tail.
The bare arm turns to the holder: an electromagnet and a ball needle on a saddle beside the arm.
The quick release slides onto the holder and clicks.
The holder leaves its saddle sideways.
The holder turns to the kit store, also in the tail.
The magnet lands on the steel disk of the kit.
Magnet on: the magnet holds the kit by the steel disk.
The kit is carried round the arm base, over the docking plane.
Away from the arm the wrist can rise: the kit goes up and over the rear wall of the gel box.
The kit is over the print seat.
The kit goes straight down through the gel onto the three seat bumps.
Magnet off: the kit stays on the seat, held by the gel; the holder lifts clear.
Tool change in the tail: the holder goes back over the rear wall.
The holder turns back round the base.
The holder slides sideways onto its saddle.
The pin on the saddle presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns to the print needle on the other side of the base.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle leaves its saddle sideways and turns toward the head.
The needle rises with the wrist and passes over the rear wall of the gel box.
The needle goes down into the gel, just inside the rear wall.
The folded newborn is printed around the kit, layer by layer, in clear silicone.
The silicone cures in the gel (75 minutes at room temperature). The print needle goes back over the rear wall to its saddle in the tail.
The holder is back on the arm: the ball needle beside the magnet now carries the air.
The holder passes over the rear wall of the gel box.
The ball needle goes to the valve on the tail end of the newborn.
Air at 450 Pa pushes the gel out of the folds through the vent in the nose; the drained newborn rises 33 mm and floats in the gel.
The needle presses the tail end down in the gel: the nose rises above the lip of the opening.
Push while inflating: every segment opens once the segment is out of the opening. All the air comes through the ball needle on the arm.
At full reach the arm holds the needle in the valve while the rest of the air goes in; the skin stretches by a quarter and the creases pull smooth.
The needle lets go; the holder goes down behind the tail end.
The holder pushes the newborn further out over the level lower lip; the front floats.
The newborn slides off the lip and floats free; the arm parks the holder and folds back into the tail.
A pocket under the forward belly has flooded and trimmed the newborn level. The small pump in the kit pushes one jet out behind: once the newborn floats, a little force moves the newborn.

checks.name: Tail prints in one piece on the H2S, with the saddles and the kit store: 253 x 314 x 336 mm of 340 x 320 x 340
Head prints in one piece, with the gel box and the lower lip: 337 x 314 x 336 mm
Everything for the tools is behind the docking plane: the saddles, the two modules and the kit store end 6 mm behind the plane; nothing hangs over or stands in the gel

The tools pass over the rear wall of the gel box: at 243 mm from the arm axis the arm can lift the tip of the print needle to 114 mm, the wall is 108 mm tall; nearer to the arm the wrist is lower (tip at 48 mm at 200 mm, 18 mm at 150 mm)
Folded arm ends 6 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof
The print needle reaches all 1440 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges

The parts dock and take the gel in the dry tank. With the gel in and 93 mm of water, the tail weighs 6.2 kg against 5.8 kg of buoyancy (with the 5 mm steel plate under the arm base and 1.28 kg of extra steel)

The filled head rests on the floor: weight 5.4 kg, buoyancy 5.1 kg. The head is hollow and mostly dry, so 1.7 kg of steel lie on its dry floor behind the gel box, under the path of the tools (a stepped block, 12 and 26 mm thick, room for 2.1 kg)
Without gel the parts would lift in the water (together 9.6 kg against 10.8 kg of buoyancy), so the gel goes in before the water, and the box is not emptied under water
The lower lip is 18 mm above the water and 3.5 mm above the gel. The docking seam is dry: the gel box starts 133 mm ahead of the docking plane and no gel reaches the seam
The gel stays in the box between births: 2.22 L, about 25 mL leave with each newborn (1.1 percent), topped up through the arm
The lip is 4 mm above the gel surface; the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm, and the folded print has already raised the level before the push
The parts for one newborn sit low, beside and behind the arm base, none higher than 122 mm; nearest to the shell 4.1 mm, nearest to the space the arm sweeps 4.0 mm. No bulkhead
Energy for one cycle about 23 Wh; the battery (three 18650 cells) holds 38 Wh: margin 1.6. The inflator runs on a battery of its own; the gel pump stands outside the tank
Silicone for one newborn: the two bores hold 92 mL, one newborn takes 83 mL

Air: the inflator of the artist fills a size 7 basketball (7.6 L, 55 kPa) in 35 s, which is 7.1 L of free air per minute; the newborn (11.2 L at 1.3 kPa) fills in about 95 s. The inflator must stop at 1.3 kPa: the preset of a tire inflator may not go that low (open question)
Every pose of the timeline is inside the official joint ranges (base -100 to 58, J1 0 to 68, J2 1 to 85 degrees)

Electromagnet (Adafruit 3872, 2.5 kg holding force): lifting force taken as a tenth, 2.5 N, through the thin silicone over the steel disk; the kit weighs 0.79 N in air and about 0.24 N in the gel: margin 3.1

Release in the gel: with the magnet off, the yield stress of the gel holds the seated kit with about 0.19 N; a remanent pull of 2 percent would be 0.05 N (estimate; a short reverse pulse makes the release certain)
The steel disk adds 2.5 g on top of the kit; the metacentric height stays 63 mm
Payload while carrying the kit: 163 g of 500 g
Force of the needle on the valve stays under the payload: peak 3.00 N of 4.91 N
The rubber ball valve grips the needle against the largest upward pull: 1.35 N of about 2 N (estimate, to bench test)
The newborn is pushed out over the level lower lip: in the middle of the push the axis of the body crosses the mouth 19 mm from its center; the mouth is 177 mm tall and 223 mm wide
Folds can be printed: story pitch 3.6 mm with one valley, pleat walls 7.1 mm apart at mid depth (limit: 1.2 mm wall plus 2 mm of gel)
Kresling stories are bistable with a barrier strain of 2.2 percent, far under the 25 percent stretch of the skin
Stretch 1.25 stays under the limit point of the membrane (1.38) and uses 4 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
Full size 428 x 301 mm against the gel chamber 337 x 314 x 336 mm: 127 percent of the length, 96 percent of the width
The newborn floats upright: metacentric height 33 mm

Draft 36 mm dry; a pocket under the forward belly floods by itself with 0.17 kg of water, which trims the newborn level and puts the jet of the pump 45 mm under water. Thrust of the one pump 30 mN at full duty; the holder pushes the tail end with at most 0.28 N
The motion settles: pitch rate in the last three seconds under 0.11 degrees per second; deepest contact at the lip 0.32 mm
Per frame penetration test over 2690 frames: deepest overlap of any pair 0.87 mm (limit 1 mm)
UNS 150U: the parent body (590 mm long, 336 mm tall) and the newborn (428 mm) in the 1470 mm inner length, with a swim run of 368 mm; water 67 L, about 203 kg filled

deriv.name: Arm base
deriv.value: fixed, 103 mm behind the docking plane, on a 5 mm steel plate on the tail floor
deriv.why: The folded DexArm ends 6 mm behind the plane. The arm stands at the very front of the tail.

deriv.name: Why the wrist is low near the arm
deriv.value: tool tip at most 18 mm high at 150 mm from the axis, 48 mm at 200 mm, 114 mm at 243 mm
deriv.why: The shoulder of the DexArm is 127 mm above its base and each link is 150 mm. J1 cannot lean back (not below 0) and J2 stops at 85 degrees, so close to the base the forearm hangs down and the wrist is low; the wrist is highest, 282 mm, with the upper arm upright and the forearm level, 249 mm from the axis. The print needle hangs 100 mm under the module head (the head must stay above the gel while the tip prints the lowest layer, 94 mm deep).

deriv.name: Gel box
deriv.value: 2.22 L of gel, flat surface at 104 mm; inside 160 x 170 x 108 mm
deriv.why: A plain box with rounded corners in the lower head: a flat floor, vertical side walls 170 mm apart, a rear wall 108 mm tall. The rear wall stands 133 mm ahead of the docking plane, 236 mm from the arm axis: the nearest place where the arm can lift the tip of the print needle over a wall of that height (6 mm of clearance). The tools cross on a ray 16 degrees off the centerline, where the wall plane is 10 mm nearer to the arm than on the centerline; that ray sets the width of the box. Variants calculated: a wall at the docking plane would have to be lower than 12 mm (the tip height there), so it would hold no gel; a shorter needle is not possible (the head would dip into the gel); a gel level low enough for a wall 100 mm from the plane (tip at 51 mm) would be 42 mm, less than the 90 mm body. The front of the box is the front wall of the head, which curves down to the floor from 399 mm to 361 mm from the arm axis, under the tapered nose of the folded print (4 mm of gel under each ring). The space between the docking plane and the box is dry floor.

deriv.name: Head
deriv.value: 337 x 314 x 336 mm outside, one print
deriv.why: After the red line. From the docking seam the roof runs forward and falls in one arc (a superellipse quarter with exponent 2.4, level only at the seam itself) to the upper lip, 274 mm above the floor. The sides close the same way from 112 mm ahead of the seam. The mouth is the open front end of this tapering head: an oval face of 177 x 223 mm leaning back 20 degrees, the upper lip 60 mm behind the lower lip. The lower lip is flat: a level shelf 38 mm long and 170 mm wide, 108 mm above the floor, from the lip back to the front wall of the gel box. Below the shelf the front wall curves down to the flat floor, which runs back to the seam. The shelf is as long as the head prints in one piece on the H2S (337 mm long); as drawn (about 105 mm) the lip would stand 176 mm from the valve the arm holds, and the head would need a second piece.

deriv.name: Tools, all in the tail
deriv.value: two saddles and the kit store, the foremost 6 mm behind the docking plane
deriv.why: The print needle hangs on a saddle 58 degrees to port, 135 mm from the arm axis; the holder (electromagnet and ball needle) 100 degrees to starboard, 130 mm from the axis; the kit waits on a tray 60 degrees to starboard. Each is carried by a short bracket from the tail wall, part of the tail print. A saddle is an L shaped ledge under the head of the module with two stops; the stem and the magnet hang free on the open side, so a module leaves sideways, on an arc round the base, at the one height (110 mm under the head) the arm can hold at these radii. The bare quick release comes up behind a module (19 mm of travel) and clicks on. With a tool on, the arm turns to the crossing ray, moves outward while the wrist rises, passes over the rear wall of the gel box and goes down into the gel. Nothing for the tools is in the head: no rack, no shelf, no well, no neck.

deriv.name: Docking
deriv.value: from behind, along the floor; a thin 4 mm ring, three magnets, dry
deriv.why: With every tool behind the plane nothing reaches into the head when the tail arrives, so the tail slides forward on the tank floor. No gel touches the seam: the gel box starts 133 mm ahead. Three DC2-N52 disc magnets on steel discs hold 161 N.

deriv.name: Tail
deriv.value: 250 mm long from the docking plane to the tip, 20.2 L, one print of 253 x 314 x 336 mm
deriv.why: After the white line. From the seam the roof curves round to the tip in one arc that still clears the arm tower (the folded arm is 314 mm tall; the arc starts 55 mm from the arm axis); the floor rises from 70 mm behind the axis; the sides close from 45 mm behind the axis. The tip is 130 mm above the floor, about the height of the top of the arm base, 147 mm behind the axis, just behind the last part. Round 6 was 334 mm long; this tail is 84 mm shorter. Volume 20.2 L (round 6: 17.8 L): the tail keeps its full width beside the arm, where the saddles and the kit store stand. Over the whole timeline the arm comes no nearer to the shell than 3 mm.

deriv.name: Tail contents
deriv.value: 5 parts, 0.46 kg, low beside and behind the arm base
deriv.why: Only what one newborn needs. Silicone: two bores of 46 mL for the 83 mL of one newborn, with a NEMA 8 class stepper. Air: the CaRSun inflator of the artist, 75 x 60 x 32 mm, flat on its side, with a battery of its own. Battery for the arm and the controller: about 23 Wh a cycle, three 18650 cells hold 38 Wh. Controller: the Raspberry Pi 5 at its real 85 x 56 mm, flat on the floor under the kit store. The gel pump is not in the tail: the gel stays in the box, and the first fill comes from a bottle and a small pump outside the tank through a port in the tail. No bulkhead, no plate. The kit is picked by a 5 V electromagnet (20 mm, 22.7 g) on the holder; the ball inflation needle stands 28 mm ahead of the magnet, with the three way stopcock on the arm, set by hand before the cycle.

deriv.name: Kit of the newborn
deriv.why: With the pump the artist owns: one AITIAO 3 to 5 V micro submersible pump, 42.6 x 23.9 x 22.7 mm, about 30 g, 0.18 A, about 100 L/h (site data, id baby_pump). Beside the pump the CodeCell C6 Drive, on top the 500 mAh cell and the steel disk for the magnet; cast in silicone on three feet (30 g, estimate). The two DFRobot pumps of the earlier rounds are gone: the kit is 29 g lighter. One pump gives one jet: the newborn swims straight. Thrust 30 mN at full duty (70 L/h through a 4 mm nozzle, estimate).

deriv.name: Printed newborn
deriv.why: The body lies from 243 mm to 393 mm from the arm axis: behind the rear wall of the box with 4 mm of gel, and inside the far reach of the print needle (393 mm at the axis of the print).

deriv.name: Full size newborn
deriv.why: Unchanged: the skin that packs into the folded volume, 0.170 m2. Kresling stories (n = 16) open the length, sixteen star pleats open the girth, a 25 percent stretch pulls the creases smooth. Unfolding at about 300 Pa (estimate), full at 1251 Pa.

deriv.name: Birth
deriv.why: After the drain the newborn floats in the gel. The arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the shelf, and pushes: the body slides out over the flat lower lip. The valve is held 328 mm from the arm axis, 180 mm high, 109 mm short of the lip; the slender tail stories open inside the mouth and carry the wide segments out. Peak force on the valve 3.00 N of 4.91 N. The tail end then still lies on the shelf, out of the water, while the front floats. The needle lets go, the holder goes down behind the tail end, where the arm reaches 79 mm further at 106 mm height, and pushes the newborn out to 46 mm short of the lip; from there the jet of the pump slides the newborn off. Friction on the shelf is taken as 0.2.

deriv.name: Water
deriv.why: The newborn draws 36 mm; the lower lip is 18 mm above the water, the gel 14 mm.

deriv.name: Time
deriv.why: First gel fill 22 min at 0.1 L per minute (later cycles only top up), print 43 min for 45 m of bead at 20 mm per second, cure 75 min, air about 95 s for 11.2 L.

deriv.name: Printing the two parts
deriv.value: tail and head, each in one piece
deriv.why: Tail: 253 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.3 kg of clear PETG at a 3 mm wall, about 15 h at 18 mm3 per second, standing on the docking face; the brackets of the saddles and the kit store need supports that break off. Head: 337 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.6 kg, about 19 h, standing on the docking face; the shelf of the lower lip and the rear wall of the gel box print with the shell.

verdict.point: 1. Head after the red curve: roof in one arc down to the upper lip, the mouth the open front end of the tapering head, a level lower lip, the front wall curving down to a flat floor
verdict.why: Roof: one arc from the seam to the upper lip at 274 mm. Mouth: an oval of 177 x 223 mm leaning back 20 degrees, the upper lip 60 mm behind the lower lip; no tube, no front face. Lower lip: a level shelf 38 mm long at 108 mm. Shorter than drawn (about 105 mm): the head is one print of 337 mm.

verdict.point: 2. Gel in a small box with rounded corners in the lower head, about 3 L or less
verdict.why: 2.22 L of gel in a box of 160 x 170 x 108 mm inside, flat surface at 104 mm.

verdict.point: 3. Everything for the tools behind the docking plane; nothing over or in the gel; no wells or necks
verdict.why: Two saddles and the kit store on brackets of the tail wall, the foremost 6 mm behind the plane. The tools cross the rear wall of the gel box from above: the wall is 108 mm tall and stands 236 mm from the arm axis, where the needle tip can be lifted to 114 mm. The price: the box starts 133 mm ahead of the seam, not right at the seam, and that stretch of the head is dry floor.

verdict.point: 4. The tail docks from behind, sliding along the floor
verdict.why: The lowering from above is removed. Three disc magnets, 161 N, on a 4 mm ring; the seam is dry.

verdict.point: 5. Tail shorter than round 6, after the white line, tip just behind the equipment
verdict.why: 250 mm from the docking plane to the tip (round 6: 334 mm), tip 130 mm above the floor. 20.2 L. One print of 253 x 314 x 336 mm.

verdict.point: 6. No separate slab in the tail
verdict.why: The bulkhead is removed; nothing stands behind the arm but the parts themselves.

verdict.point: 7. Equipment far less, far smaller, low, under and beside the arm; material for one newborn
verdict.why: 0.46 kg in 5 parts (round 6: 0.75 kg): bores of 46 mL for one newborn, three cells (38 Wh), the inflator of the artist, the Raspberry Pi 5 at 85 x 56 mm, a small stepper. No gel pump in the tail. The highest part ends 122 mm above the floor.

verdict.point: 8. The pump of the newborn is the AITIAO micro submersible pump of the artist
verdict.why: One pump of 42.6 x 23.9 x 22.7 mm, 30 g, in a kit of 46 x 46 x 34 mm and 81 g (before: 110 g with two DFRobot pumps). Newborn 0.317 kg, draft 36 mm dry; thrust 30 mN at full duty, top speed in the run 55 mm/s. After the needle lets go, the holder pushes the tail end 79 mm further out over the lip (0.28 N); the jet does the rest.

verdict.point: The arm at the very front of the tail, on a fixed base
verdict.why: Axis 103 mm behind the docking plane; all 2690 poses of the timeline are inside the joint ranges.

verdict.point: The parent body rests on the tank floor; only the newborn floats
verdict.ok: yes, with steel in the head
verdict.why: In 93 mm of water the tail weighs 6.2 kg against 5.8 kg of buoyancy; the head, now mostly dry inside, weighs 5.4 kg with the gel and 1.7 kg of steel on its floor, against 5.1 kg.
Printed 150 x 90 mm, full size 428 x 301 mm, 11.2 L, unchanged: 73 percent of the length of the whole parent body (590 mm).

limits: Open points on the parts: a tire inflator may not stop as low as 1.3 kPa; the force of the electromagnet through the silicone skin and its release in the gel need a bench test; the product pages of the inflator, the stopcock and the ball valve were read by the artist and the coordinator, not opened from here.

Estimates, to measure: the mass of the DexArm (2.4 kg), the power of the DexArm while moving (12 W), the mass of the inflator, the flow of the AITIAO pump through a nozzle (70 of its 100 L/h), the mass of the cast kit, the module head (30 x 40 x 52 mm), the seal of the cup, the flow of gel through a 3.5 mm tube, the pressure that opens the folds (300 Pa), the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), the pump curve of the kit pumps, friction at the lip (0.2).

How the official joint angles J1 and J2 map onto the link meshes is an assumption, as on the full version. The DexArm specification page could not be opened again from here on 21 November 2026; its numbers are those used on the full version.

The valve is a soft boss on the tail cap and the nozzle stays vertical while the body pitches by up to 36 degrees: this needs a bench test. So does the drain of the gel from the folds, and whether a fold packed this tightly prints and opens as drawn.
The force on the valve is a quasi static estimate from slices: weight, buoyancy in the gel and in the water, the lip with friction, yield drag.

The newborn is drawn rigid with one soft droop where the body leaves the opening; a real skin at 300 Pa also wrinkles. In the force estimate the unfolded part outside is limp at that droop: the lip, the hull front and the water carry that part, and the arm steers only the part still inside. Friction at the gel wet lip is taken as 0.2.
The swim is a straight run on one jet; the speed comes from an estimated flow through the nozzle. The page for the AITIAO pump is a reseller page for the pump class; no primary page exists.

In the mouth the order in which the segments open is scripted: the three slender tail stories first, each wide segment once past the lip. A real skin under one pressure opens everywhere at once and presses on the wall of the mouth; whether the body then slips out as drawn needs a bench test.
Overlap is measured from sampled points (4 to 11 mm apart) against exact surfaces, so a figure can be about 1 mm off.

read.birth_text: Quasi static estimate from slices. Peak 3.00 N; the payload of the DexArm is 4.91 N. The needle pushes forward and down; the gel carries the body inside, the lip and the water carry the body outside.
read.tank_text: The tank is the Ultum Nature Systems UNS 150U, a rimless low iron glass tank of 1500 x 600 x 600 mm with 15 mm glass (the longest stock length under 1.8 m; no stock tank is 1.3 m). The parent body, 590 mm long and 336 mm tall, stands on the floor at one end; 93 mm of water (67 L) leave the lip of the opening 18 mm above the water and give the newborn 748 mm of open water ahead. Filled as shown the tank weighs about 203 kg.
